name: tool_hint_confidence
description: Tasks labelled with the catalog tools that answer them (empty: none does). The catalog is two the agent-harness benchmarks use: its tool-choice sets (examples/06_scenarios/tool_choice.py: store operations; tests/live/heldout.py: IT help desk, travel) and the memory service's context-latency catalog (benchmark/context_latency.py). kind: match (a tool answers it), near_miss (the catalog's domain, but no tool does it: an action no tool takes, a figure no tool returns), unrelated (small talk, general knowledge, a question about the user). split halves the set by a hash of the task: constants are fitted on dev and reported on test.

catalog.name: store_overview
catalog.description: A store's dashboard at a glance: the week's sales, stock on hand, sell-through and service level, as store totals. Use for a general picture of how a store is doing. It has no figures by style: for excess stock, lost sales or allocations by style, use the tools made for those.

store.description: The store's id, such as S12.

catalog.name: excess_stock
catalog.description: The styles holding more stock than they will sell at a store (overstock), with the units over target, largest first.

store.description: The store's id, such as S12.

catalog.name: lost_sales
catalog.description: The sales a store lost to stock-outs, by style, largest first.

store.description: The store's id, such as S12.

catalog.name: allocatable_stock
catalog.description: The units available to allocate (ATA) in the warehouse, by style, largest first.

catalog.name: allocation_history
catalog.description: The allocations made to a store in the past, newest first.

store.description: The store's id, such as S12.

catalog.name: app_help
catalog.description: Where in the app to do something: the menu path and the steps. Use when the user asks how or where to do something in the app, not for data.

task.description: What the user wants to do, such as "create an allocation".

catalog.name: store_demand
catalog.description: A style's weekly demand and stock on hand at a store, and the weeks of cover they give (fewer weeks: the store runs out sooner).

style.description: The style's id, such as ST-101.

catalog.description: Create a stock rule for a style at a store: the minimum and maximum units it keeps. A change: a person approves it before it is made.

catalog.name: desk_dashboard
